note: GIMS dashboard PIPELINE cases for autoSQL (T-46): what a stored record becomes between instances.data and the screen (key copies, the _noun_type tag, the forgiving field lookup, the sort order, the where filter). A superset of GIMS's tests/fixtures/expr_vectors.json: the same top keys and case keys, plus `kind` (expr | record | sort | filter) and `autosql` (what autoSQL's shipping compiler and runtime do on the case). Expected values are hand-authored from GIMS's code and confirmed by GIMS's own Python pipeline (parity/check_gims_pipeline.py); do NOT regenerate them from either side. A divergence is kept and explained, never deleted. Source of truth: autoSQL parity/; GIMS pins a vendored copy by sha256.

autosql.why: SQL reads instances.data as stored. GIMS's get_noun_items adds a copy of every top-level key with spaces and underscores swapped (api/iostore/nouns.py _normalize_row) before anything evaluates, so the copy exists only in GIMS. Fix side: the adapter (T-37) applies the same copies before the row reaches SQL, or the compiler resolves a key to its copies.

cases.note: Both stored keys copy to 'a b c'; setdefault keeps the first one processed. In Postgres mode GIMS receives keys in jsonb order (shorter first, then bytewise): 'a b_c' precedes 'a_b c', so its value wins. In SQLite mode insertion order would decide instead, so the two modes can disagree.
